plan.notes: Transcribed 2026-11-13 from the official Southern Utah University 2026-2027 General Catalog (current edition, catoid=28) Nutrition - Allied Health Emphasis program page (poid=10861) and its linked official degree map, 'Nutrition Degree Maps (2026-2027)', tab 'Allied Health (Campus)' (the workbook's Index lists Online as N/A for this program), last updated/reviewed July 31, 2026. Semester placement is the university's official sample 4-year campus academic plan (SUU Program Maps, 2026-2027), which the source itself labels a guide only; students confirm specifics in Degree Works with a Student Success Advisor. Every semester's courses sum to the map's printed semester total (16/13/15/14/16/15/16/15) and the plan to the catalog's printed Total Credits, BS Degree: 120. Per the catalog, all courses must be passed with a C (2.0) or better to be counted in the major, courses over 10 years old will not be accepted in the major, and the program requires MATH 1040 Statistical Inference or MATH 1050 College Algebra. The catalog Curriculum (59 credits) is exercised exactly: Nutrition Core 36 (the seven named NFS courses 19 + Chemistry Track 10 + Math Requirement 4 + Nutrition Electives 3) and Restricted Elective Courses 23 (the map's four restricted rows total exactly 23). The map exercises Chemistry Track B (CHEM 1210/1215/1220/1225) over Track A (CHEM 1110/1115/1120/1125) and MATH 1050 for the Math Requirement (the slot carries MATH 1040 as the other option); the Fall Year 4 'Major Core Elective' row, which prints no course number, is the Nutrition Electives complete-one slot and carries NFS 4040 and NFS 4480. The catalog's Bachelor of Science Degree Requirement (12 credits) notes that a portion may be met by fulfilling the General Education Core and Breadth Areas, so the catalog blocks do not sum arithmetically to 120. The map spells the CHEM 1225 lab title 'Principels of Chemistry II Lab'; the catalog title is recorded. Map free rows total 21 credits and free upper-division rows 21, recorded as printed (the catalog prints no free-elective figure).
